text:
To continue to meet user needs we regularly review our releases to look at the existing content, as well as opportunities from new data and new or emerging user requirements.

Read about Changes made to DWP statistics between April 2020 and March 2025.

The changes delivered since April 2025 across our releases are set out in 10 themes:

Benefit statistics

Children, Families and Bereavement

Employment support schemes

Health, disability and care

Housing and heating

Income and living standards

Pensions and older people

Spending, fraud and error

Transparency

Work and unemployment

1. Benefit Statistics

Annual DWP Benefits Statistics Compendium

This is a compendium publication that brings together key statistics on benefits administered by the department to provide a complete picture of DWP responsibility. Statistics on Housing Benefit (administered by Local Authorities) and Universal Credit are also included.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the August 2025 release the following was included:

inclusion of a new flag, Gap between Housing Benefit (HB) and Rent, indicating whether a customer’s HB payment covers their rent. This flag has been added to the Stat-Xplore HB Point in Time Caseload table.

From the February 2026 release the following was introduced:

a new breakdown in Stat-Xplore showing accommodation type enabling users to apply the new accommodation type indicator to view how many claimants in the monthly Housing Benefit (HB) caseload statistics are living in specified accommodation (SA) and temporary accommodation (TA)

three geography variables have been removed from the Housing Benefit (HB) caseload and flows datasets on Stat‑Xplore

From the September 2026 release, the following was changed:

DWP Benefits Statistics (including Benefit Combinations) moved to an annual statistical release including an annual release of statistical data on Stat-Xplore with a new name that reflects this – “Annual DWP Benefits Statistics Compendium”

2. Children, Families and Bereavement

Child Maintenance Service statistics

The Child Maintenance Service statistics report on the quarterly performance of the Child Maintenance Service. Child maintenance is financial support between separated parents to help with the everyday living costs of looking after children.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the June 2026 release the following was introduced:

introduced an additional category, “Collect and Pay – no liability due,” to improve the clarity and robustness of the published statistics. This new category separately identifies cases where no payment is expected, preventing them from being grouped with genuine non-payment cases and ensures a more accurate reflection of compliance. Further detail on this new category is available via the CMS Children Stat-Xplore dataset and the CMS Arrangements Stat-Xplore dataset.

Children in low income families: local area statistics

The Children in low income families: local area statistics - GOV.UK (CiLIF) provides information on the number and proportion of children living in low income families. The statistics complement and should be viewed as a companion release to the Households Below Average Income (HBAI) statistics which provide survey estimates of children in low income households at a national and regional level.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the March 2026 release the following was introduced:

following completion of the discovery work and a user consultation, After Housing Costs (AHC) local area child poverty statistics are now included in the publication, given the importance of AHC metrics for the Child Poverty Strategy

revisions to the back-series were made to update the absolute low-income reference year from financial year ending (FYE) 2011 to FYE 2025. The integration of benefits administrative data into the Family Resources Survey (FRS) (from FYE 2022 in March 2026 and from FYE 2019 in summer 2026) means the current absolute low‑income reference year (FYE 2011) was no longer suitable

Separated families statistics

The Separated families statistics - GOV.UK uses the Family Resources Survey (FRS) and Households Below Average Income (HBAI) data. It provides statistical estimates relating to separated families and their child maintenance arrangements.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the March 2026 release the following was introduced:

An update was made to the absolute low-income reference year from FYE 2011 to FYE 2025. The integration of benefits administrative data into the Family Resources Survey (FRS) (from FYE 2022 in March 2026) means the current absolute low‑income reference year (FYE 2011) was no longer suitable

Universal Credit (UC) childcare element statistics

The Universal Credit childcare element statistics to February 2026 provide information on claimants receiving support, amounts paid, and breakdowns including the number of children supported and ethnicity.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the May 2026 release, the following change was introduced:

extended the statistics to include the number of children supported by the UC childcare element and added ethnicity breakdowns to support childcare reform, child poverty analysis, and equality assessments

3. Employment support schemes

Access to Work statistics

The Access to Work statistics provide statistics on approvals, payments and expenditure for Access to Work provision.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the October 2025 release, the following developments were included:

Transitional Employer Support Grant (TESG) formerly published as part of Work Choice statistics and Access to Work Plus (AtW+) as categories for breakdowns by element type

figures for Non-contracted Provision - Non-contracted provision is defined as total Access to Work expenditure excluding expenditure on Assessments and the Mental Health Support Service (MHSS) which are contracted elements delivered through external providers therefore funded differently to other Access to Work support

in addition to primary medical condition, provided a broader medical condition categorisation including “Musculoskeletal conditions” and “Mental Health Conditions”

average payment amounts received per customer across the financial year

a breakdown of the Support Worker types within the Support Worker element

breakdowns by employment characteristics; employer size and employment status which includes a category for people undergoing a Supported Internship

Connect to Work statistics

The Connect to Work statistics provide official statistics on the Connect to Work employment programme. Connect to Work is a key part of the Pathways to Work offer of support to help individuals with disability, health conditions, and other complex issues into employment.

Changes delivered since April 2025

The first release, published on 11 June 2026 included:

new official statistics on the Connect to Work programme

referrals to Connect to Work

starts to Connect to Work

first earnings from employment

job outcomes achieved

Work and Health Programme

The Work and Health Programme (WHP) predominantly helps disabled people, as well as the long-term unemployed and certain other priority groups (known as early access groups) to enter into and stay in work.

From November 2018, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has released Official Statistics about WHP. These provide information on a regular basis about the number of:

referrals to WHP

starts to WHP

job outcomes

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the May 2025 release, the following additional breakdown was included:

pioneer statistics – 12-month measures for first earnings from employment and job outcomes measures

From the May 2026 release, the following was introduced:

pioneer statistics - further breakdowns on first earnings from employment and job outcomes measures for Pioneer have been published, e.g. 24-month figures from May 2026 onwards

the frequency of the publication has reduced from biannual to annual, the next release will be taking place in February 2027, and this will be the final release

4. Health, disability and care

Universal Credit Health statistics

The Universal Credit Health statistics cover the number of people on Universal Credit with a health condition or disability restricting their ability to work.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the December 2025 release the following additional breakdowns were included:

claimants transitioning from Employment Support Allowance (ESA). An ESA transition is defined as a claimant who had an open ESA spell or an ESA spell that had closed within 90 days of the Universal Credit (UC) Work Capability Assessment (WCA) decision date or, for the caseload, the recorded UC health start date. This will include Move to UC cases and natural migration through change in circumstances and dual claims

From the June 2026 release the following was introduced:

inclusion of individual ages 66 to 69 on StatXplore (replacing the 65+ age group)

From the September 2026 release the following changes were introduced:

the statistics were renamed Universal Credit (UC) Health statistics (previously known as UC Work Capability Assessment statistics)

new breakdowns were introduced for higher and lower Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity (LCWRA) award amounts and Severe Condition status

Health Assessment Statistics: Personal Independence Payment and Work Capability Assessments

The Health Assessment Statistics: Personal Independence Payment and Work Capability Assessments include statistics on Personal Independence Payment (PIP) and Work Capability Assessments (WCA) assessment volumes and channels in Great Britain.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the September 2026 release the following was introduced:

these statistics were published for the first time covering PIP assessments and WCAs completed in Great Britain between January 2021 and July 2026

5. Housing and heating

Housing Benefit Debt Recoveries statistics

The Housing Benefit Debt Recoveries statistics include statistics on the amount of Housing Benefit that is overpaid to claimants, the overpayments recovered and amounts written off.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the September 2025 release the following was introduced:

a new graph and narrative, which shows recovery and write-off as a proportion of available debt, for additional context to the existing total amounts of recovery/write-off in the publication. This provides a more transparent picture of recovery against the total outstanding and identified over time

These statistics were released for the final time on 2 September 2026, covering data for the financial year ending 2026.

Housing Benefit: statistics on speed of processing

The Housing Benefit: statistics on speed of processing include statistics on the average number of days to process a new Housing Benefit claim or a change in circumstance of an existing claim.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the January 2026 release the following was introduced:

two new tables showing numbers of new claims and average speed of processing times in specified accommodation (SA) and temporary accommodation (TA)

These statistics were released for the final time on 29 July 2026, covering data for quarter 4 financial year ending 2026.

Support for Mortgage Interest statistics

The Support for Mortgage Interest statistics count the number of households who are currently in receipt of the support, as well as the number who have received an SMI loan since April 2018.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the September 2025 release the following were also introduced:

publication moved from a quarterly release to a bi-annual release schedule, publishing in March and September of each year

a statistical publication to add relevant context and description of recent trends to aid user’s interpretation of the statistics

a median measure for the average weekly loan amount variable to help users identify where large back payments may cause the average (mean) loan amount to appear higher in some breakdowns

Winter Fuel Payments statistics

The Winter Fuel Payment statistics present tables and commentary on Winter Fuel Payment recipients and households.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the September 2025 release the following was introduced:

statistics are available for the first time on Stat-Xplore covering the last 3 years of Winter Fuel Payments

the statistics now include a measure of the proportion of the pension population who are beneficiaries of Winter Fuel Payment

From the September 2026 release the following changes were introduced:

to reflect changes in Winter 2025 to 2026 eligibility and Winter Fuel Payment (WFP) policy, changes were made to WFP metrics, including changes to payment amounts, the cessation of the proportion of pensioners metric, and the introduction of additional management information metrics on opt-outs

6. Income and living standards

Family Resources Survey

The Family Resources Survey (FRS) is a continuous household survey which collects information on a representative sample of private households in the United Kingdom. Detailed information is recorded on each respondent: their incomes, from all sources including self-employment, housing tenure, caring needs and responsibilities, disability, expenditure on housing, education, pension participation, childcare, family circumstances and child maintenance.

The primary purpose of the FRS is to provide the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) with data to inform the development, monitoring and evaluation of social welfare policy.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the March 2026 release the following were introduced:

the variable EDUCQUAL was revised in March 2025 for the financial year ending (FYE) 2023 and FYE 2024 FRS datasets, the FYE 2024 households below average income (HBAI) dataset and Stat-Xplore. In the March 2026 release, these revisions have been applied to FYE 2022 FRS and HBAI datasets, and the FYE 2023 HBAI dataset and Stat-Xplore. Earlier years will not be updated due to data deletion requirements under UK GDPR

five questionnaire changes approved through the annual consultation have been implemented in the FRS financial year ending (FYE) 2025 questionnaire. These are included in the main FRS publication, and Stat‑Xplore

a new table in the Savings and investment chapter (Table 7.13) is available, showing households by level of savings and investments and the ethnic group of the head of household, based on a three‑year average for financial year ending (FYE) 2023, FYE 2024 and FYE 2025. The data needed for this table have been collected for three years, allowing publication consistent with the standard approach for ethnicity reporting

this dataset includes the Census 2021 update to the 2011 Rural-Urban classification, for England and Wales. This allows users of the Household Food Bank Usage tables to view this breakdown with the most recent indicator available, thereby giving an up-to-date perception of the rural-urban status of an area and its relationship to food bank usage

Households below average income (HBAI) statistics

The HBAI statistics report information on living standards in the UK based on household income measures. The report incorporates estimates of average incomes, income inequality, and the prevalence of low income households. HBAI uses data from Family Resources Survey (FRS).

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the March 2026 release the following were introduced:

four HBAI trend tables (5.5trends, 5.6trends, 6.5trends and 6.6trends) were updated so that going forward they are not affected by changes to the State Pension age (SPa) over time. This followed feedback from expert users and ensures the time series remains comparable and free from distortions caused by shifting SPa boundaries

new Deep Material Poverty (DMP) tables were included. Users will need these following the publication of the Child Poverty Strategy and related ad hoc statistics in December 2025, as DMP becomes one of the headline indicators for tracking progress against the Strategy

two new After Housing Cost (AHC) charts were added: real-terms incomes AHC by percentile (the AHC equivalent of chart 1_1) and weekly net equivalised household income AHC by percentile (the AHC equivalent of chart 1_2). These respond to repeated user requests for AHC versions of existing Before Housing Cost charts and improve transparency and consistency across the publication, particularly given the increasing emphasis on AHC measures

the variable EDUCQUAL was revised in March 2025 for the financial year ending (FYE) 2023 and FYE 2024 family resources survey (FRS) datasets, the FYE 2024 HBAI dataset and Stat-Xplore. In the March 2026 release, these revisions were applied to FYE 2022 FRS and HBAI datasets, and the FYE 2023 HBAI dataset and Stat-Xplore. Earlier years have not been updated due to data deletion requirements under UK GDPR

an update was made to the absolute low-income reference year from financial year ending (FYE) 2011 to FYE 2025. The integration of benefits administrative data into the family resources survey (FRS) (from FYE 2022 in March 2026 and from FYE 2019 in summer 2026) means the current absolute low‑income reference year (FYE 2011) was no longer suitable

Income Dynamics statistics

Income Dynamics statistics - GOV.UK statistics provides estimates of the rates of persistent low income, as well as estimates of mobility across the income distribution, including low income entry and exit rates and analysis on the events associated with these movements.

Income Dynamics statistics uses data from Understanding Society, a longitudinal survey run by the Institute for Social and Economic Research at the University of Essex.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the March 2026 release the following was introduced:

inclusion of the Understanding Society General Population Sample boost in the March 2026 publication

Income-related benefits: estimates of take-up

The Income-related benefits: estimates of take-up statistics provide estimates of take-up for income-related benefits within the entitled pensioner population. The pension age benefits covered are Pension Credit (PC) and Housing Benefit (HB).

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the November 2025 release the following was introduced:

inclusion of Family Resources Survey (FRS) transformation data which incorporates improved linking of administrative data to the FRS, to better identify those in receipt of PC or HB

more extensive calibration, which improves the representativeness of the weighted survey sample and ensures a consistent approach with other statistics

From the October 2026 release the following was introduced:

inclusion of new Official Statistics in Development on estimates of take-up of Universal Credit (UC) (or equivalent benefits), this initial release reports on financial year ending (FYE) 2024 and FYE 2025 estimates

7. Pensions and older people

Pension Credit applications and awards

The Pension Credit applications and awards statistics cover the number of weekly Pension Credit claims received, claims cleared and claims awarded.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the September 2025 release the following additional breakdowns were included:

the geographic distribution of applications and awards – by country, region, local authority, and Westminster parliamentary constituency

From the May 2026 release the following change has been made:

the frequency of the publication will reduce from quarterly to annual

Workplace Pension Participation

The Workplace pension annual statistics include detailed breakdowns of the number of savers, and the amount of savings.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the July 2025 release the following was introduced:

new reporting on median contribution rates as a percentage of pay, by sector and gender

more detailed statistics on the decumulation phase, including more granular breakdowns by age

different industry groupings aligned with other publications from HMRC/ONS (for example ASHE), backdated for the entire series

more granular age bands and employer size categories, for example 22 to 25, 25 to 29, and so on

reporting on all employees in certain groupings, not just those eligible for Automatic Enrolment

including breakdowns by Parliamentary Constituency

From the July 2026 release the following was introduced:

new tables showing Automatic Enrolment opt-out rates and stopped saving rates by age, gender and earnings, providing more detailed insight into participation and saving behaviours across demographic groups

expanded analysis of pension decumulation products by type, age and gender, giving users a greater understanding of how different demographic groups access different types of pension savings in later life

8. Spending, fraud and error

Benefit Cap statistics

The Benefit Cap statistics provide statistics on households affected by the benefit cap.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the September 2025 release the following was introduced:

Universal Credit (UC) capped household statistics will only be refreshed for the latest 2 years – older data will be frozen

Housing Benefit (HB) capped household data will only be available via Stat-Xplore. The bulletin will no longer include HB narratives, graphs, or tables. This reflects the low number of capped HB cases as UC replaces HB for working-age customers

From the March 2026 release the following was introduced:

The remaining ODS tables will be moved onto Stat‑Xplore. For the March 2026 release, both ODS tables and Stat‑Xplore versions will be published side by side, before switching to Stat‑Xplore only from June 2026. This change is intended to make the statistics easier for users to navigate by bringing all Benefit Cap data into one place.

Fraud and error in the benefit system

DWP pays benefits to over 20 million people. It is necessary to estimate how much money the department incorrectly pays, either through over or under payment. The overpayments or underpayments can occur for a number of reasons such as:

claimant error

official error

a consequence of fraud

This annual publication presents estimates of the rates of these over and underpayments as well as their respective causes (fraud and error). Benefits measured as part of DWP’s fraud and error analysis include:

Universal Credit (UC)

Housing Benefit (HB)

Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)

Pension Credit (PC)

Personal Independence Payment (PIP)

Jobseeker’s Allowance (JSA)

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the May 2025 release, the following changes were introduced:

change to how we deal with Living Together overpayment cases where both claimant and alleged partner are benefit claimants

change to the proxy measure we use for Winter Fuel Payment (WFP) Fraud and Error due to the change in WFP eligibility rules

change to New Case Factors

change to causal Link Non-Residency Fraud Adjustment

change to Error Code Framework Adjustments

From the May 2026 release, the following changes were introduced:

change to the “failure to provide evidence adjustment”

change to Winter Fuel Payment proxy measurement

consistency of recording Fraud and Error and Unfulfilled Eligibility where a change of circumstances does not impact the claimant’s award

Unfulfilled Eligibility in the benefit system

To get welfare benefits people need to meet certain eligibility criteria and the amount of money they receive depends on their circumstances. Sometimes people tell us the wrong information or do not tell us when their circumstances change. Reporting accurate information and providing evidence may change the amount of benefit people are eligible for and in some circumstances, they may be eligible for more money. However, we cannot calculate the correct amount unless people tell us accurately about their circumstances. This means that people are not eligible for increases in the amount of money they receive until we have the correct information.

The publication Unfulfilled eligibility in the benefit system estimates how much extra money benefit claimants could be getting if they told us accurately about their circumstances. These people are already getting some money on a certain benefit but may not be getting all the money they could be eligible for on this benefit – we call this unfulfilled eligibility.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the May 2025 release, the following changes were introduced:

change to New Case Factors

change to how we deal with Living Together unfulfilled eligibility where both claimant and alleged partner are benefit claimants

change to Error Code Framework Adjustments

From the May 2026 release, the following change was introduced:

consistency of recording Fraud and Error and Unfulfilled Eligibility where a change of circumstances does not impact the claimant’s award

9. Transparency

DWP Complaint Statistics

The DWP Complaints Statistics are Official Statistics in Development. The increased data available as part of this Official Statistics publication increases the transparency of DWP complaints and DWP customer experience.

Changes delivered since April 2025

The first release, published on 16 December 2025, included:

complaints received, closed, and upheld by each business area, as well as categorisation of the root cause

Independent Case Examiner (ICE) quarterly data on received complaints about DWP, complaints accepted for investigation, cleared complaints, and complaint outcomes broken down by business area

10. Work and unemployment

Get Britain Working: Labour Market Insights

New quarterly Official Statistics in development on Get Britain Working: Labour Market Insights aims to continue expanding on publicly available content to tell a broad story of the labour market.

Changes delivered since April 2025

The first release, published on 30 October 2025, included:

Universal Credit (UC) customer employment and journeys

UC customer into-work rates

analysis of local labour markets

The second release, published on 29 January 2026, included:

updated core labour market statistics for Great Britain

new analysis focusing on young people, including employment outcomes and sector patterns

insights into Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET) rates across English regions

contextual analysis of local labour market types and their impact on youth employment, health, and inactivity

The third release, published on 30 April 2026, included:

into‑work rates for people on Universal Credit in the ‘Searching for work’ conditionality regime

English regional not in education, employment or training (NEET) rates

updated Get Britain Working outcome metrics

new statistics covering skills and employment across industrial sectors

a methodological update to previously published statistics applied going forward

The release published on 29 October 2026 included:

geographical analysis of labour markets

Move to Universal Credit (UC) statistics

The Move to UC statistics are published quarterly and show the number of people who have been sent managed migration notices inviting them to claim UC.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the August 2026 release the following was introduced:

key headline Move to UC statistics are now included within the quarterly UC statistics publication

quarterly Move to Universal Credit statistics continue to be available through Stat-Xplore

The employment of disabled people

The Employment of Disabled People statistics give detailed analysis and breakdowns of the number of disabled people in employment.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the November 2025 release the following additional breakdowns were included:

characteristics of those with “other” health conditions and disabilities

characteristics of disabled people with Autism and severe or specific learning difficulties

overlapping health conditions

labour market status of disabled people by labour market cluster

characteristics and flows into employment by disability status of young people not in education, employment or training (NEET)

benefit and employment history of disabled people using Family Resources Survey (FRS) and Registration and Population Interactions Dataset (RAPID) linked data

Universal Credit (UC)

The Universal Credit statistics (UC) have been developed to provide information on people and households receiving UC, as well as data on claims and starts to UC.

The main statistical release for claims, starts, people and households on UC is published quarterly. This is supplemented by monthly updates of data for people on UC. All data are available via Stat-Xplore, interactive maps and dashboard, and the quarterly statistical publication which is published on GOV.UK in HTML format.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the July 2025 release the following additional breakdowns were included:

inclusion of breakdowns of immigration status and nationality – this will be incorporated into quarterly releases going forward

From the February 2026 release the following was introduced:

new Stat-Xplore measure to identify people that have transitioned from legacy benefits to UC as part of the ‘Move to UC’ programme

From the May 2026 release the following was introduced:

expanded the employment indicator to include self-employment

statistics are now only released on a quarterly basis each May, August, November, and February in line with the existing UC statistics quarterly schedule. Each quarterly release includes a further 3 months of data for each measure, accompanied by a statistical publication. Individual month data points, will continue to be available via Stat-Xplore, however only released at quarterly intervals accompanying the quarterly publication. To confirm, there will no longer be monthly publication of UC Official Statistics on Stat-Xplore

UC statistical series have been brought into improved sequencing alignment, using consistent reference points

provisional monthly estimates have been removed, reducing the need for frequent revisions and providing users with more robust, finalised UC Official Statistics

Universal Credit and Child Tax Credit claimants: statistics related to the policy to provide support for a maximum of 2 children

The Universal Credit and Child Tax Credit claimants publication shows the number of claimants (single or joint adult households with any dependent children or young people) affected by the policy to provide support for a maximum of two children, and eligible for a positive Universal Credit or Child Tax Credit award. It includes statistics relating to the exceptions to the policy.

Changes delivered since April 2025

From the July 2025 release the following additional breakdowns were included:

the age of the youngest child in the household

demographic information of households, such as gender and ethnicity

receipt of other benefits, such as Disability Living Allowance (DLA) and Personal Independence Payment (PIP)

whether households are also affected by the benefit cap

the conditionality group of households

These statistics were released for the final time on 8 July 2026.

National Insurance number allocations to adult overseas nationals entering the UK

The National Insurance allocations statistics show a count, by individual nationality, of the number of new (flow) National Insurance numbers registered to adult non-UK nationals, irrespective of the length of stay in the UK. The statistics are not a count of the number of adult non-UK nationals currently residing in the UK.

Changes delivered since April 2025

Following the May 2026 release the following was implemented:

the statistics moved to be published annually in September, covering data to the end of the previous March representative of the financial year. There was no release in August 2026 as data up to March 2026 (covering the whole of Financial Year 2025 to 2026) was published in May 2026
